Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass MAP that breaks the security/compliance gates into discrete milestones and acceptance checks. Summary here so it's easier to scan:

1) Intake & evidence exchange (Week 0–1)
   - FinPulse provides SOC 2 attestation and SIG/CAIQ export
   - Redwood shares SOC scope summary, controls mapping, and a short attestation note

2) Technical validation (Week 1–2)
   - Demo/sandbox access for FinPulse security team (short-lived tenant, read-only telemetry)
   - Confirm telemetry/trace retention and availability windows (we'll provide sample logs)

3) Legal & DPA negotiation (Week 1–4, parallel)
   - Redwood legal reviews FinPulse redline; propose counterpoints on retention carveouts and incident notification windows

4) Final review & signoff (Week 4–6)
   - SOC 2 artifacts reviewed, SIG questionnaire reconciled, DPA executed, onramp checklist closed

Proposed acceptance criteria (gate-level):
- SOC 2: most recent Type II report within 12 months OR completed gap remediation plan with timeline if older.
- SIG: completed CAIQ export and answer set; open items not to exceed 5 medium/critical controls without mitigation plan.
- DPA: Data residency clause addresses EU/US routing for covered data; retention windows specified and agreed.
- Sandbox: FinPulse able to ingest 1k synthetic events and verify retention/traces for 30 days in staging.

I'm attaching: FinPulse_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx, SOC2_Prelim_Attestation.pdf (Redwood summary), and our suggested DPA redline (DPA_redline_v3.docx).

If the timeline above looks OK, propose we kick off a 30-minute MAP walk-through tomorrow at 10am PT. I can add Jonas (ops) and Kimberly (legal) for the DPA points.

Best,
Priyom Das

Priyom —

Thanks for the draft. A few legal/contract points to call out so we keep the MAP realistic:

- Retention windows: FinPulse's ask for 7 years on audit logs is high but not unheard of. We should propose a split approach:
  * Security audit logs (for compliance) — retain 7 years but with tiered access and export tooling (cost recovery)
  * Application-level event data / analytics — default 2 years with option to extend per customer via addendum

- DPA redlines: I flagged three priority items in the attached redline: subprocessor disclosure cadence, breach notification timing (we propose 72 hours post-detection, not post-investigation), and deletion/return semantics for backups.

- SIG/CAIQ: ops should provide the exported answers and map to our SOC controls; Jonas can own the technical reconciliation and propose mitigations for any medium/critical gaps.

- Sandbox: we should offer a staging token with limited data retention and auditing enabled; ops to instrument a telemetry retention view for FinPulse to validate.

I'll start a parallel thread with Legal to surface the DPA counterpoints; for the MAP meeting tomorrow 10am PT I'll cover the DPA and retention framing.

Kimberly Park
